fields.summary: Autonomous plan run (no owner) for change set 01M78T0, filed after the 2026-11-12 performance report (~/orchestrator/perf-2026-11-12/report-prospective.md, recommendation 1: run 01M787SV ran the full make check 4 times, ~20-25 min each on the test lock, mostly after changes that touched only .rhiza/). The planner read internal/api/ship_gate.go (the gate already passes at once on a head recorded as Gated in the ship state, keyed on the commit, so any render or log commit reruns it), the ship-change workflows and the sibling change set 01M78RM (gate switches on only for repeated named flakes). Three questions went to the arbiter in one call: which intent to serve, what the reuse key is, and how scoping stays language-neutral. The arbiter's Decision local-gate-reuse-and-scope: serve m35-ship-40m; record the hash of the passing head's tree with top-level .rhiza/ left out and pass at once when a clean HEAD has the same non-.rhiza/ tree (.rhiza/ is checked on every push by the pre-push check); the gate command stays the project setting rhiza.ship.localGate, run with RHIZA_GATE_BASE (merge-base with origin/main) and RHIZA_GATE_HEAD in its environment, and Rhiza's own repo supplies a script that scopes go test to changed packages, their reverse dependencies, the affected testscripts and make self-check, falling back to the full suite; no Go-specific scoping in the shipped product. The planner chose the affected testscripts as the changed txtar files plus those named TestScripts/<name> in the change set's leaf acceptance checks, and a reuse that also requires the same gate command.
fields.title: Plan of 01M78T0: a passing local gate is reused
